text_en: Very soon after this, Lysias, the king’s guardian and kinsman, who was in charge of the government, being vexed at what had happened,
text_cn: 此后不久，王的亲戚和监护人并国务总理里息雅，对所遭遇的事，异常愤恨，

text_en: gathered about eighty thousand infantry and all his cavalry and came against the Jews. He intended to make the city a home for Greeks,
text_cn: 便募集了八万步兵及所有的骑兵，出发进攻犹太人，企图将圣城作为希腊人的居所；

text_en: and to levy tribute on the temple as he did on the sacred places of the other nations, and to put up the high priesthood for sale every year.
text_cn: 向圣殿征税，像对其他各国的寺庙一样；并且每年高价出售大司祭的职位。

text_en: He took no account whatever of the power of God, but was elated with his ten thousands of infantry, and his thousands of cavalry, and his eighty elephants.
text_cn: 他毫不想天主的威能，而只信赖他的几万步兵，数千骑兵和八十匹象。

text_en: Invading Judea, he approached Beth-zur, which was a fortified place about five stadia from Jerusalem, and pressed it hard.
text_cn: 侵入犹太之后，逼近离耶路撒冷约三十二公里的一个要塞贝特族尔，倾全力围攻。

text_en: When Maccabeus and his men got word that Lysias was besieging the strongholds, they and all the people, with lamentations and tears, prayed the Lord to send a good angel to save Israel.
text_cn: 玛加伯与部下听说他围攻那堡垒，便与民众一同叹息流泪，恳求上主派一位好天使来拯救以色列。

text_en: Maccabeus himself was the first to take up arms, and he urged the others to risk their lives with him to aid their kindred. Then they eagerly rushed off together.
text_cn: 玛加伯自己首先拿起武器，然后激励众人跟他去冒险拯救同胞；众人都自告奋勇与他前去。

text_en: And there, while they were still near Jerusalem, a horseman appeared at their head, clothed in white and brandishing weapons of gold.
text_cn: 他们离耶路撒冷不远，有位身穿白衣，手挥金武器的骑兵出现，作他们的前锋。

text_en: And together they all praised the merciful God, and were strengthened in heart, ready to assail not only humans but the wildest animals or walls of iron.
text_cn: 他们一致称扬仁慈的天主，个个勇往直前，不但准备冲锋杀敌，而且还敢与最凶猛的野兽搏斗，冲破铜墙铁壁。

text_en: They advanced in battle order, having their heavenly ally, for the Lord had mercy on them.
text_cn: 他们既得上主垂怜，从天上获得助战者，就列阵前进，

text_en: They hurled themselves like lions against the enemy, and laid low eleven thousand of them and sixteen hundred cavalry, and forced all the rest to flee.
text_cn: 冲向敌人如猛狮一般，击杀了步兵一万一千，骑兵一千六百，迫得其余的人都望风而逃，

text_en: Most of them got away stripped and wounded, and Lysias himself escaped by disgraceful flight.
text_cn: 大半负伤弃甲逃命，连里息雅自己也得抱头鼠窜，才得苟全性命。

text_en: As he was not without intelligence, he pondered over the defeat that had befallen him, and realized that the Hebrews were invincible because the mighty God fought on their side. So he sent to them
text_cn: 但他并不是个愚昧人：当他回想自己所遭遇的失败，便知希伯来人是不可战胜的，因为有全能的天主与他们共同作战；

text_en: and persuaded them to settle everything on just terms, promising that he would persuade the king, constraining him to be their friend.
text_cn: 于是派遣使者，去同犹太人说和，立平等的条件，且许下尽力劝国王与他们做朋友。

text_en: Maccabeus, having regard for the common good, agreed to all that Lysias urged. For the king granted every request in behalf of the Jews which Maccabeus delivered to Lysias in writing.
text_cn: 玛加伯为顾全公共的利益，就接受了里息雅所提出的一切，王也批准了玛加伯为犹太人向里息雅书面所要求的各项条件。

text_en: The letter written to the Jews by Lysias was to this effect: “Lysias to the people of the Jews, greetings.
text_cn: 里息雅给犹太人所写的函件如下：“里息雅祝犹太人民安好！

text_en: John and Absalom, who were sent by you, have delivered your signed communication and have asked about the matters indicated in it.
text_cn: 你们的使者若望及阿贝沙隆呈递下附的函件，请求批准所列的事项。

text_en: I have informed the king of everything that needed to be brought before him, and he has agreed to what was possible.
text_cn: 凡应转呈君王的，我已禀呈；凡是可允准的，他一概允准了。

text_en: If you will maintain your goodwill toward the government, I will endeavor in the future to help promote your welfare.
text_cn: 若你们对政府仍保持友好，今后我必尽力为你们谋求幸福。

text_en: And concerning such matters and their details, I have ordered these men and my representatives to confer with you.
text_cn: 关于这些及其余详细事项，我已吩咐你们的使者和我的特派员与你们会商。

text_en: Farewell. The one hundred forty-eighth year, Dioscorinthius twenty-fourth. ”
text_cn: 祝你们健康！一四八年，‘雕斯苛洛’月二十四日。”

text_en: The king’s letter ran thus: “King Antiochus to his brother Lysias, greetings.
text_cn: 王的谕文如下：“安提约古王祝兄弟里息雅安好！

text_en: Now that our father has gone on to the gods, we desire that the subjects of the kingdom be undisturbed in caring for their own affairs.
text_cn: 自从先父归于诸神以后， 我们愿意所属人民，自管其国，不受骚扰；

text_en: We have heard that the Jews do not consent to our father’s change to Greek customs, but prefer their own way of living and ask that their own customs be allowed them.
text_cn: 我们也听说犹太人不满先父令他们随从希腊风俗， 而愿保守自己固有的生活方式，并且要求遵守自己法律的许可。

text_en: Accordingly, since we choose that this nation also should be free from disturbance, our decision is that their temple be restored to them and that they shall live according to the customs of their ancestors.
text_cn: 其实，我们很愿意这民族不受骚扰，决意将圣殿交还他们，准许他们按照祖先的习例度日。

text_en: You will do well, therefore, to send word to them and give them pledges of friendship, so that they may know our policy and be of good cheer and go on happily in the conduct of their own affairs. ”
text_cn: 所以，你更好派使者到他们那里去，与他们和好，好使他们认清我们的意思，安心乐意处理自己的事务。”

text_en: To the nation the king’s letter was as follows: “King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews and to the other Jews, greetings.
text_cn: 王给犹太民族所颁的诏书如下：“安提约古王祝犹太参议院与其他的人民安好！

text_en: If you are well, it is as we desire. We also are in good health.
text_cn: 如果你们安康，那正是我们的希望，我们也很平安，

text_en: Menelaus has informed us that you wish to return home and look after your own affairs.
text_cn: 默乃劳向我们呈报，说你们愿意回乡，从事己业。

text_en: Therefore those who go home by the thirtieth of Xanthicus will have our pledge of friendship and full permission
text_cn: 因此，凡在‘散提苛’月三十日以前回家的，一概得享平安。

text_en: for the Jews to enjoy their own food and laws, just as formerly, and none of them shall be molested in any way for what may have been done in ignorance.
text_cn: 并允许犹太人像昔日一样，享用自己规定的食物，遵守自己的法律；如果有人无意做了什么错事，谁也不可干涉。

text_en: And I have also sent Menelaus to encourage you.
text_cn: 此外，我又派默乃劳前去慰问你们。

text_en: Farewell. The one hundred forty-eighth year, Xanthicus fifteenth. ”
text_cn: 谨此祝你们健康！一四八年‘散提苛’月十五日。”

text_en: The Romans also sent them a letter, which read thus: “Quintus Memmius and Titus Manius, envoys of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greetings.
text_cn: 罗马人也寄给犹太人一封公函，其原文如下：“罗马人的使者昆突默米，提突玛尼祝犹太人民安好！

text_en: With regard to what Lysias the kinsman of the king has granted you, we also give consent.
text_cn: 王的亲人里息雅与你们商定的事，我们也表示赞同。

text_en: But as to the matters that he decided are to be referred to the king, as soon as you have considered them, send some one promptly so that we may make proposals appropriate for you. For we are on our way to Antioch.
text_cn: 对于那些他认为应请示国王的事，在你们仔细考虑以后，即刻派一人来，使我们能依照你们的利益去建议，因为我们快要起身到安提约基雅去。

text_en: Therefore make haste and send messengers so that we may have your judgment.
text_cn: 请急速派几个人来，叫我们知道究竟你们有什么意见。

text_en: Farewell. The one hundred forty-eighth year, Xanthicus fifteenth. ”
text_cn: 谨此祝你们健康！一四八年‘散提苛’月十五日。”
